The varying widths of the confidence intervals directly reflect the escalating uncertainty associated with longer time horizons. Moving to the 1-week horizon, the interval expands to 114.45 to 118.95. Despite the comprehensive nature of these intervals, certain unforeseen events or "black swan" risks could push outcomes beyond these boundaries. These might include sudden and severe global economic crises, unexpected major geopolitical conflicts, rapid and drastic shifts in government fiscal or monetary policy, or unprecedented natural disasters that significantly disrupt markets. Additionally, extreme swings in market sentiment, such as a widespread panic selling detached from fundamentals or irrational speculative bubbles, could also lead to outcomes well outside the projected ranges. For an individual asset, an unanticipated corporate scandal, a groundbreaking technological breakthrough, or a severe regulatory crackdown could similarly cause an extraordinary deviation from the forecasted path.
